newsitem.title: USA: CyberAmerica says option holder detained.
newsitem.headline: CyberAmerica says option holder detained.

text.p: CyberAmerica Corp said on Friday that Allen Wolfson, who had an option to buy 25 percent of the company, had been detained for alleged U.S. federal securities violations.
A company spokesman said he did not think Wolfson had exercised the option.
CyberAmerica said that short-term operations should not experience severe repercussions from Wolfson's detention, but that it could not yet predict the full impact of the event.

Wolfson was never named an officer or director of CyberAmerica, but the company said he had significant influence and "control," as defined by U.S. Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, over company affairs.

The company, which develops and sells Internet goods and services, said it had not received a full account of Wolfson's alleged activities, but had no reaseon to believe the company or any empoyees were involved.
CyberAmerica also provides financial consulting services and buys, manages and sells real estate.
The company said it would disclose any further information it received.
